forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 21%. Quiet 24 hours — no fresh capability announcement crossing the 3+ leading-researcher attestation threshold. Hassabis's Google I/O 'foothills of the singularity' framing (20 May, reported by Semafor) reinforces a 'we're getting closer but not there' narrative rather than a YES-triggering declaration. Anthropic policy head Jack Clark's 60%-by-2028 recursive-self-improvement claim is a notable forward indicator but not a resolution event. OpenAI's $122B funding round at $852B valuation deploys more capital toward AGI but, per the renegotiated Microsoft contract, the term 'AGI' has already been displaced by capability gates — making a clean public declaration less, not more, likely. 31 months to deadline; time decay continues to dominate.
forecasts.base_rate: Major paradigm-defining technology claims with sub-3-year horizons resolve YES <20% historically. AI Impacts 2023 survey median for HLMI clusters 2040-2047. Metaculus community ~25% by 2027, ~50% by 2031. Kalshi contributors ~40% on OpenAI AGI by 2030, but this question's resolution (public lab announcement OR 3+ leading researchers) is stricter.

factors_up.factor: Continued frontier capability gains (Gemini 3.5, Anthropic agentic scaling, GPT-5.5)
Anthropic's Clark 60% recursive-self-improvement-by-2028 framing suggests insider conviction
OpenAI $122B raise compresses capital-availability constraint on race dynamics

factors_down.factor: OpenAI/MS contract renegotiation removed 'AGI' clause — deprecates the term for high-stakes resolution
No researcher consensus near YES threshold; published surveys still cluster 2040+
31 months remaining is short relative to typical capability-to-attestation lag
Hassabis's 'foothills' framing is the opposite of a declaration

key_uncertainties: Whether 'AGI' as a term survives the OpenAI/MS renegotiation or fragments into capability benchmarks
Whether a lab unilaterally declares AGI for funding/marketing reasons before researcher consensus
Speed of agentic capability gains over the next 12 months
update_triggers: Any public lab claim of AGI achievement
Coordinated statement from 3+ leading-lab researchers
METR task-horizon benchmark >1 month
Scaling plateau or compute constraint signal

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp to 25%. Fresh coverage of McKinsey's late-2025 200-role cut (now widely reported as a warning signal for the sector) and LinkedIn Economic Graph data showing ~25% of entry-level consulting/finance postings now require AI fluency (vs <5% two years ago) reinforce the trajectory. Big Four (Deloitte/PwC/EY/KPMG) have all rolled out staff AI assistants and trimmed back-office headcount. The directional pressure is unmistakable, but reaching a ≥33% sectoral decline by end-2030 still requires sustained acceleration — current cuts are <5% of headcount and concentrated in support roles, not revenue-generating engagements. Engagement value per consultant may be rising even as junior pyramids shrink, partially offsetting revenue declines.
forecasts.base_rate: Industry-wide 33% contraction over a 5-6 year window from a single technology shock is rare. Historical analogues: travel agencies (~50% decline 2000-2015 from internet); print publishing (~35% revenue decline 2006-2012); legal services associate hiring (~15% from doc review automation). Most analogues took longer than the deadline implied here.

factors_up.factor: Big-name layoffs (McKinsey 200; Big Four ongoing) signal sector-wide structural shift
LinkedIn graph: 25% of junior postings require AI fluency — entry pyramids genuinely under pressure
AI assistants now standard at Big Four — productivity gains will flow to billable hour compression
Bloomberg Intelligence's 200k bank job estimate sets a precedent for analogous consultancy outlook

factors_down.factor: Current cuts <5% of headcount; from there to 33% requires aggressive ongoing acceleration
Demand for AI-implementation consulting is genuinely rising — substitution offset
Sector revenue lags employment by 2-3 years; even with layoffs, revenue decline by end-2030 less likely
Resolution requires '2+ credible analyses' attributing the decline primarily to AI — high bar

key_uncertainties: Whether the McKinsey cuts mark inflection point or one-off restructuring
How much of the impact lands by 2030 vs. 2032-2035
Whether the AI implementation consulting boom fully offsets traditional engagement compression
update_triggers: Big Four announces layoffs >5% of headcount
Sector revenue decline reported in Statista/Source Global Research benchmarks
Major consulting firm publicly attributes >20% efficiency gain to AI
Counter-evidence: consulting headcount rises in 2026-2027

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 2%. YouGov 4-5 May poll (Ref 25, Lab 18, Con 17, Grn 15, LD 14) and PollCheck 7-poll moving average (Ref 27.9%, Lab 18.7%, Con 18.3%, Grn 13.6%, LD 13.0%) both confirm a sustained Reform UK lead approaching ~10pp over Labour. Labour is now in third or even fourth place on some polls, with only its under-50 base holding firm. Under FPTP the seat translation can still surprise (Reform's vote is geographically spread), but with the GE deadline at December 2029, Labour faces a structurally hostile environment with no sign of a turning point. Movement would require either Reform implosion, government-led economic turnaround, or a major opposition coalition strategy — none currently in evidence.
forecasts.base_rate: Incumbent governments polling sub-20% in mid-term recover to largest-party status in <15% of historical cases (UK + comparable Westminster systems). 1992 Major recovery and 2019 Johnson swing are exceptions; 1979 Callaghan and 2010 Brown more typical.

factors_up.factor: FPTP rewards geographic efficiency; Reform vote may waste in safe-Lab city seats
Up to 4 years to GE — long window for political recovery
Tactical voting on right (Ref/Con) may split anti-Labour seats

factors_down.factor: Reform 10pp+ lead in headline polling — sustained, not transient
Labour approval near historical lows for an incumbent at this point
Greens (15%) and LDs (14%) eating Labour's progressive base
No identified strategy to win back over-50s, a key seat-rich demographic

key_uncertainties: When the GE will actually be called (early-2029 vs. late-2029)
Whether Reform's organisational capacity holds through a full national campaign
Whether external shocks (geopolitical, economic) reset the political landscape
update_triggers: Labour vote share recovers above 25% in 7-poll average
Reform leadership crisis or major scandal
Election called within 6 months
Major economic turnaround attributable to government policy

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 78%. The 2035 deadline gives 9 more years vs. 31 months, which transforms the profile from 'tail event' to 'modal outcome' given current trajectories. Today's signals — Hassabis's 'foothills' framing, Clark's 60% recursive-self-improvement-by-2028, OpenAI's $122B raise — all push in the same direction on this longer horizon: more capital, more conviction, more compute, more researcher belief. The dominant downside risk on the 2035 question isn't capability but resolution mechanics: whether the term 'AGI' survives as a coherent target rather than fragmenting into benchmark-specific definitions. With OpenAI/MS deprecating the term, that risk has structural weight.
forecasts.base_rate: Metaculus community ~75% by 2035; Kalshi ~70%; AI Impacts 2023 survey 10th percentile for HLMI ~2030-2035. The 9-year horizon dominates the resolution probability.

factors_up.factor: 9-year horizon: even slow capability growth saturates the threshold
Anthropic recursive-self-improvement signal (60% by 2028) implies post-2028 capability acceleration
Capital deployment at scale (OpenAI $122B, Anthropic $43B ARR) sustains R&D pipeline through 2030s
Multimodal/world-model progress (Hassabis remarks) addresses key AGI bottlenecks

factors_down.factor: 'AGI' as term may fragment into benchmark-specific definitions, frustrating resolution
Capability ≠ public declaration; researcher coordination remains uncertain
Possible scaling plateau or compute/energy constraint in late 2020s
Policy/regulatory friction may slow disclosure of AGI-level systems

key_uncertainties: Whether the resolution language ('AGI') holds up against industry term-shifting
Whether scaling laws continue to deliver capability gains past current paradigm
Geopolitical disruption to compute supply chains
update_triggers: Public AGI declaration from any leading lab
Industry shift toward 'transformative AI' / capability-gate language replacing 'AGI'
Compute scaling plateau evidence
Major policy intervention restricting capability disclosure

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 7%. AEI's 1 May and 8 May Taiwan updates report PLAN deployments in South China Sea and West Pacific tied to Balikatan 2026 exercises — significant signalling, but described as 'information operations' rather than escalation. The PLAN's Luzon Strait posture is intended to demonstrate first-island-chain breakout capability but is explicitly characterised as not indicative of wartime intent. The December 2025 Justice Mission drills remain the high-water mark for blockade rehearsal, but no new escalation beyond exercise pattern in the past week. Risk profile remains: high baseline tension, sustained rehearsal cadence, no observed mobilisation gradient that would precede actual blockade execution. 43 months to deadline.
forecasts.base_rate: Major-power initiated blockade/invasion against an established democracy with US security commitments occurs in <5% of analogous 5-year windows since 1949. Closer reference class (Taiwan-strait crisis years 1954, 1958, 1996): no escalation beyond exercises.

factors_up.factor: Sustained exercise cadence (Justice Mission 2025, May 2026 deployments) normalises blockade posture
PRC explicitly responding to multi-nation exercises (Balikatan 2026) suggests reactive escalation dynamic
Xi's 2027 modernisation deadline keeps military timeline under political pressure

factors_down.factor: AEI characterisation: 'information operation', not escalation
PRC economic position vulnerable to sanctions; blockade is enormously costly
No observed civilian/logistics mobilisation that typically precedes major operations
US Indo-Pacific deterrent posture remains robust (Balikatan, ongoing FONOPs)

key_uncertainties: Whether Xi accepts the cost-benefit of blockade given Russia-Ukraine sanctions precedent
Trajectory of Taiwan internal politics (2028 election)
Whether US deterrence credibility shifts materially in next 24 months
update_triggers: PLA reservist mobilisation or amphibious lift posture change
Major China-Taiwan trade or diplomatic rupture
Taiwan independence declaration or major sovereignty signal
US deterrence credibility crisis

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Up 3pp to 10%. ONS confirmed April 2026 CPI annual rate at 2.8%, down sharply from 3.3% in March — a 0.5pp single-month decline driven primarily by housing/household services (electricity and gas), with the housing component falling from 4.3% to 3.0%. Core CPI also fell from 3.1% to 2.5%. The path to sub-2.0% is becoming more credible: with 8 monthly prints remaining (May 2026 through December 2026), a further 0.8pp decline is now within reach if energy base effects continue and services inflation moderates. Still the modal outcome is for CPI to stabilise around 2.3-2.6%, given sticky services. But the probability mass on a single sub-2.0% month has materially shifted upward.
forecasts.base_rate: Single-month sub-2% prints in disinflation cycles occur in ~30% of post-shock periods over a 6-12 month window. The recent UK trajectory mid-2024 to early-2025 saw briefly sub-2% before resurging.

factors_up.factor: April 2026 CPI 2.8% (down from 3.3%) — largest single-month deceleration in 12 months
Housing component dropped 1.3pp; further energy base-effect support expected through Q3 2026
Core CPI now 2.5%, below headline — services inflation finally moderating

factors_down.factor: Services inflation still sticky; 0.8pp further decline needed to cross threshold
BoE April MPR expected CPI to remain above 2% throughout 2026
Wage growth remains above level consistent with 2% target
Only 8 monthly prints remain before deadline

key_uncertainties: Whether energy price disinflation continues or reverses
Whether services inflation breaks below 3% in coming months
Whether wage settlements in autumn 2026 round reaccelerate inflation
update_triggers: May or June CPI print below 2.5%
BoE rate cut signalling sub-2% near-term path
Energy price re-acceleration
Wage growth sustained above 5%

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 98%. Sacra now estimates Anthropic ARR at $43B as of April 2026, with credible projections of $43-45B by late Q2 2026 (note: this is gross-basis recognition under ASC 606 for partner-channel consumption via Bedrock/Foundry/Vertex). OpenAI confirmed at $24B ARR ($2B/month) in April, with Sacra-estimated $25B by February. Combined April 2026 ARR is already approximately $67-68B — within striking distance of the $70B threshold seven months before the deadline. Anthropic's reported quarter-over-quarter growth (~$9B end-2025 to $43B April 2026) combined with OpenAI's monthly cadence makes >$70B by end-Q4 2026 essentially the modal outcome barring catastrophic disruption.
forecasts.base_rate: Combined ARR growth trajectory of two leading AI labs over 8 months exceeding 5% from a $67B base has very high empirical support given observed monthly growth rates. Reference class: hyperscaler revenue growth never previously declined more than 10% over a single quarter outside macro recession.

factors_up.factor: Combined ARR already $67-68B in April — only $2-3B further needed
Anthropic ARR grew ~5x in 4 months — trajectory implies easy crossing
OpenAI confirmed monthly cadence ($2B/month) → $24B+ growth path
Reporting will likely be available — Bloomberg, FT, Information all tracking

factors_down.factor: Resolution requires 'most recent credible reporting' of Q4 2026 — possible timing/source ambiguity
ARR methodology differences (Anthropic gross vs OpenAI confirmed) could affect aggregation interpretation
Macro disruption (compute outage, regulatory action) could compress growth

key_uncertainties: Whether Q4 2026 figures are publicly disclosed by 31 December resolution date
Whether resolver accepts gross-basis Anthropic ARR or requires net adjustment
Black-swan disruption to either firm
update_triggers: Q3 2026 ARR disclosure from either firm
Major outage, regulatory action, or compute crunch
Methodology shift in revenue recognition by either company
Unexpected slowdown in enterprise adoption

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Unchanged at 38%. OBR March 2026 EFO forecasts headline GDP growth 1.1% in 2026 and 1.6% in 2027, with real GDP per person growing 1.1% per year between 2026-2030. Aggregate potential output growth is 0.1pp lower than November forecast due to weaker net inward migration offsetting marginally higher investment. This implies the structural baseline going into the 2030s sits near the threshold, not comfortably above it. The 1.5% headline target requires either (a) population/migration recovery, (b) a productivity surge, or (c) a sustained AI-driven productivity dividend that the OBR has not yet priced. None of these is the modal path, but each has plausible upside. Result: this question stays a coin-flip-with-downward-tilt.
forecasts.base_rate: UK rolling 10-year GDP growth average exceeded 1.5% in ~55% of historical decades, but post-2008 trend has been ~1.3%. Productivity-driven shifts >0.5pp over a decade occur in ~25% of cases.

factors_up.factor: 2027 OBR forecast 1.6% suggests baseline near the threshold
AI-driven productivity dividend not yet priced into 1.1% per-person forecast
Investment level marginally higher in latest OBR forecast
Strong Q1 2026 print (+0.6%, best-in-G7 alongside US) suggests near-term resilience

factors_down.factor: OBR aggregate potential output growth revised down 0.1pp on weaker net migration
Per-person growth 1.1% forecast implies headline ~1.3% baseline
Post-2008 trend ~1.3% — beating it requires structural change
10-year average is mean-reverting; one bad year (recession) drags substantially

key_uncertainties: Whether AI productivity dividend materialises in macroeconomic data
Whether net inward migration rebounds from current trajectory
Whether the next 2030s recession is deep enough to drag the decade average
update_triggers: OBR or IFS upward revision to medium-term potential growth
Major productivity surprise in 2027-2029 prints
Migration policy reversal raising labour supply
Deep 2030s recession (multi-quarter)
